rationale: B wins because it knows where the bodies are buried: mobile billing, net-versus-gross fees, IPO attribution, named server owners, and payout data. A has a solid lead angle in "Discord undercuts Apple and Google, charging creators a 10% cut instead of 30%," but B makes the same angle safer by asking "whether the subscriptions flow through mobile in-app purchase at all — which is where the 30% actually bites." A is usable; B is the one that keeps a founder from getting corrected by a reporter in the first follow-up email.
gaps_in_A: "Discord just gave server owners a way to get paid — it won't say how much they'll make" implies Discord is withholding data; the update only says no creator-earnings data exists yet because the program is new.

"Discord's move signals monetization is coming for the whole server, not just the streamer" is a category thesis doing push-ups in the mirror. One launch does not prove a whole-server shift without comparable examples.

"Confirmation of exactly which transactions the 10% applies to" is directionally right but too soft; the decisive proof is whether mobile subscriptions still trigger Apple or Google billing and payment-processing fees.
"Does 'premium content' on gaming servers include anything gambling- or loot-box-adjacent?" may be a smart lawyerly worry, but nothing in the supplied facts points there.
gaps_in_B: "unpaid volunteer community managers" is an invented labor frame. The facts say server owners can charge; they do not say those owners were unpaid volunteers.
"Discord is turning 200 million users into a subscription business before an IPO" overstates the base. Discord has 200 million MAU, not 200 million plausible paying subscription customers.
"The prevailing belief is that a 200-million-user base plus a cheap take rate is an obvious win" is a strawman unless you can source that belief. B admits it is inferred, but it still leans on it.
"Run the detector first" is debatable in a 24-hour launch window. The more urgent next move is to get the mobile-billing answer and one named server owner before pitching.
